A braid of silver bulbs looped in a long uneven drape across three beams, each bulb carrying a bright spark at its heart so the whole braid pulses faintly, one bulb tied back to its cord with a mismatched ribbon of orange silk.

A net of luminous spore-sacs stretched between two rafters at a slight diagonal, breathing brighter and dimmer in slow alternation, one loose cap caught in the mesh where it fell from the bundle above.

Bundles of upside-down stems budding again in the warmth, small white buds tight at their tips, hung at four different heights on a single crooked nail so they stagger down one corner of the ceiling like a rough stair.

A long chain of dried moon-shaped caps thinning from fat full rounds at one end to paper slivers at the other, the fattest caps holding an amber inner glow, the chain hung off-centre so it grazes the top beam on one side.
A rope of knotted roots strung the length of the room, one knot glowing warm copper where it was tied, the rest dark and weathered, the whole rope sagging lower at its midpoint than either end.

Seed-pods on individual strings drifting slowly sideways against the draught, each pod a pale gold and faintly rattling, the strings cut to seven different lengths so the pods hang in a loose wandering scatter across the upper dark.

A mat of purple-flowered stems mounted on a bent twig frame and turning slowly on a single central cord, the purple deepening as each face catches the lamplight below, one corner of the mat curling away from its frame.

Sheaves of grasses bound at the stalk with raw cord, their seed-heads sparking pale white when the draught moves them, four sheaves hung in a loose cluster at uneven drops with a fifth sheave shoved higher than the rest.
A garland of berries looped in two long swags of unequal length, each berry glowing red from within like a coal, the shorter swag bunched where its cord was knotted crooked and left that way.

Strips of bark curling and uncurling gently on their lines, each strip a different width, catching a faint silver sheen as they open and releasing it as they close, one strip propped partly open on a thin twig wedged behind its cord.

Bundles wrapped in birch-bark cones hung at four mismatched heights, a thread of gold light leaking from each tip and falling in short bright drips into the air below, one cone left unwrapped and bare at its hook.
A hanging tray of drying moss with tiny mushrooms sprouting along its outer rim, the mushroom caps a pale violet, the tray propped level on a short stick at its low corner holding the moss steady.

A swag of flowers frozen in mid-fall on their stems, petals arrested at every angle as if stopped in the moment of dropping, the whole swag casting small coloured shadows that hold still even when the swag sways.

A chain of apple-rings gone amber-transparent like lenses, each ring catching the light below and throwing a small warm circle onto whatever is under it, one ring hanging at a twist so its circle spins slowly on the shelf top.

Thistle-heads on a long cord, holding a faint blue static charge so they lean toward each other in pairs and odd groups, the cord itself hung at an angle so one end rides a full hand higher than the other.
A cluster of beeswax bags hung on short uneven cords, each bag glowing softly gold with whatever is sealed inside, one bag drifted out of line and resting lightly against the bundle beside it.

A trailing vine still carrying several shrivelled leaves and one fresh impossible bloom, the bloom a deep copper-orange and fully open, the vine pinned to the ceiling beam in three places at irregular intervals so it bows between them.

Strips of dried petal threaded on fine wire in long vertical runs of unequal length, the petals translucent rose and amber, each wire spinning at its own slow pace so the columns of colour cycle in and out of the light.

A row of small baskets hung from a crossbeam, one basket lifting a full hand's breadth higher than its hook as though pulling toward something above, the rest at ordinary heights, all filled with dried caps in graduated sizes.

A long rack of feathers suspended on a horizontal pole at two uneven cords, the feathers catching and holding the lamplight so they seem to smoulder copper and bronze, one empty clip on the pole where a feather was taken.

A curtain of dried moon-fern fronds hung in overlapping layers at different depths, each frond carrying a faint silver edge that brightens when two fronds brush, a single frond pinned back with a small wooden toggle to keep it from the one beside it.

A cascade of luminous seed-strings dropped from a central iron ring, each string a different length so the seeds hang in a rough cone shape, the seeds glowing pale green and rotating on their threads at uneven speeds.

A broad hoop strung with caged wisps at mismatched heights, the wisps a cool blue-white, their light swinging across the dried bundles nearby, the hoop itself hung off its hook at a slight tilt so one side rides lower.

A braid of roots and dried stems wound together in a thick rope, wrapped at intervals with cord in three different colours, glowing faintly amber between the wrappings, one wrapping done up crooked so the cord loops before it tightens.

A wide loose swag of dried herb bundles in mixed sizes, bound together with raw twine at three uneven points so the swag bellies lower in the middle, the smallest bundle in the group giving off a thin persistent thread of pale blue smoke.

A long braid of silver bulbs looped in a slow descending spiral from beam to beam, each bulb holding a bright spark at its heart, the lowest bulb hanging a full hand's breadth lower than the rest, its cord tied off in a crooked knot.

A net of luminous spore-sacs stretched between two beams, each sac breathing faintly brighter then dimmer on its own rhythm, one dried cap fallen from a neighbouring string and caught in the mesh, dimpling it gently downward.

A chain of apple-rings gone amber-transparent strung at a shallow diagonal across the far corner, each ring acting as a small lens that throws a warm oval of light onto the beam above, the chain fastened at one end with a mismatched ribbon of blue silk.

A swag of waxy flowers frozen in mid-fall along their stems, petals arrested at every angle, the whole garland dusted in a faint silver that catches every shift of lamplight and throws brief sparks across the ceiling.

A rope of knotted roots descending from a single iron hook, one knot glowing amber where it was tied, the others dark and woody, the whole rope drifting a few degrees off vertical as though the glow inside it gives off a gentle push.

A row of small woven baskets suspended at staggered heights on cords of differing lengths, each basket packed with drying moss and pale puffballs, one basket drifted quietly out of line so it hangs closer to the wall than the others.

Sheaves of silver-green grasses bound in three loose bundles and hung at uneven heights, their seed-heads sparking small cold blue flickers each time the draught moves them, the middle bundle tied shorter than intended so it rides higher than its neighbours.

A mat of purple-flowered stems laced into a circular frame, turning in a slow lazy rotation as though on a hidden spindle, the underside of the mat paler and faintly luminous, spinning its violet shadow across the rafters above.

Thistle-heads threaded on fine copper wire in a loose cluster, each head carrying a faint blue static charge so they all lean fractionally toward each other, one head on the outermost wire leaning away from the rest as though resisting.

Garlands of berries looped between three hooks at descending heights, the berries glowing red from within like cooling coals, the rightmost loop hanging lower than any hook should allow, its extra length pooling softly in a small luminous heap.

Bundles wrapped in birch-bark cones, seven of them hung on a shared line at irregular intervals, a thread of gold light leaking from each tip, one cone missing its wrapping so the dried contents are visible through the gap and still glowing regardless.

A hoop strung with little caged wisps bobbing at mismatched heights on uneven threads, their pale green light swinging arcs across the dried bundles crowded nearby, one hook on the hoop left bare where something was recently lifted free.

A hanging tray of drying moss slung on four cords, tiny mushrooms sprouting in a soft fringe along the tray's rim as it dries, the tray propped level at one corner on a short forked stick jammed between cord and beam.

Strips of amber bark curling and uncurling gently on their line like slow breathing, each strip gone translucent at its thinnest curve so the lamplight passes through and casts warm curved shadows on the ceiling above, one strip curled tighter than the others.

A rack of iridescent feathers pinned to a drying bar, each feather catching and holding lamplight in a different colour along its vane, the bar itself hanging crookedly from cords of unequal length so the whole rack tilts toward the left.

Seed-pods on fine strings drifting sideways in a slow collective glide against the draught, each pod rattling faintly with something small and luminous inside, one string longer than the rest so its pod trails lower and brushes the bundles hanging below.

A long chain of dried moon-shaped caps descending from thick to paper-thin at the far end, the thickest caps holding a warm inner glow that fades to a bare silver shimmer in the thinnest slivers, the chain hung at a steep diagonal.

Beeswax bags in a cluster of nine, each bag glowing softly with the warm amber of whatever is sealed inside, the bags hung at three different heights on cords of braided red fibre, one bag carrying a small painted picture of a leaf on its face.

A trailing vine looped across two beams, most of its leaves shrivelled and papery and catching the light like foil, one fresh impossible bloom open at the lowest point of the loop, its petals so vivid they look wet, a blank scrap of bark tied to its stem.

Bundles of upside-down stems wrapped in linen, several of them budding again in the warmth of the ceiling, small pale shoots pressing out through the cloth at the base of each bundle, the linen ties on two bundles gone loose and unravelling slowly.

A braid of dried cap-stems threaded with glass beads at long intervals, the beads acting as lenses that focus lamplight into tight bright points on the beam below, one bead cracked clean through and throwing its light in a doubled image.

Garlands of translucent seed-wings strung in a wide arc from rafter to rafter, each wing catching the faintest air current and lifting slightly before settling, the garland's highest point fastened with a knot done up crooked so one side hangs lower.

A cluster of dried moon-cap stems bundled together at the top and fanning open below, their cut ends each carrying a faint phosphorescent ring of blue-white, the whole cluster hanging lower on one side where the binding cord has slipped down the hook.

Loops of golden wire strung with dried amber discs at irregular intervals, each disc refracting the overhead light into small rainbow slivers across the ceiling, the wire looped an extra turn around the left-hand hook so that side rides a knuckle higher.

A wide swag of layered dried petals pressed flat and strung in overlapping scales like fish-scales, the whole panel shifting between deep rose and pale copper as the lamplight moves, one petal at the lower edge curling loose and dangling on a single thread.

A long braid of silver bulbs looped across three beams at uneven drops, each bulb carrying a bright spark at its heart that pulses faintly out of step with its neighbours, one bulb wrapped in a mismatched ribbon of red where the braid was mended.

A net of luminous spore-sacs stretched corner to corner overhead, each sac breathing brighter then dimmer on its own slow rhythm, a single dried cap fallen from a higher bundle resting in the mesh like a dark coin.

Bundles of stems hanging upside-down in odd clusters of three and five and two, budding again at their cut ends in the warmth, small pale shoots curling downward, one bundle tied with a knot pulled so crooked the whole thing hangs tilted.

A rope of knotted roots descending in a long diagonal from rafter to hook, one knot glowing amber where it was tied as though the tying itself remembered heat, the rope swinging a half-turn whenever the draught shifts.

Sheaves of tall grass bound at staggered heights along a single cord, their seed-heads throwing sparks of cold white light each time the draught moves them, one sheaf shorter than the rest and propped out from the beam on a forked stick.

A chain of dried moon-shaped caps thinning from fat rounds at one end to paper slivers at the other, each cap rimmed in a faint silver luminescence, the chain drifting slowly sideways against every visible current of air.

Garlands of small berries looped in three uneven swags at different heights, each berry glowing red from within like a banked coal, one swag longer than the others and dipping low enough to brush the top of the highest shelf.

A hanging tray of drying moss slung on mismatched cords at two heights so it tilts, tiny mushrooms sprouting in a crooked line along its lower rim as it dries, the moss itself a deep living green against the pale ceiling.

Strips of birch bark on separate lines curling and uncurling gently as the temperature shifts, a thread of gold light leaking from each rolled tip, one strip half-unrolled and showing a faint painted mark pressed into its inner face.

A swag of flowers held frozen in mid-fall along their stems, petals arrested at every angle of opening and closing, the whole length casting faint violet shadows upward onto the rafter above, one stem tied back to the beam with a scrap of bark.

Bundles wrapped in birch-bark cones at three different heights along the same beam, gold light leaking from each tip in a thin thread, the cones swaying on different lengths of cord so they never align, one cone facing inward toward the beam.

A mat of purple-flowered stems suspended on four cords and turning slowly like a mobile above the centre of the room, its rotation catching the lamplight across each tiny floret in sequence, one corner of the mat dipping lower where a cord has stretched.

A chain of apple-rings gone amber-transparent like lenses, hung in a long irregular loop from two hooks at uneven heights, light passing through each ring and throwing small warm circles onto the bundles below, one ring missing from the middle of the sequence.

Thistle-heads on short individual strings at different drops, each carrying a faint blue static that makes them lean toward their nearest neighbour, the lean growing stronger near the centre of the cluster where four heads almost touch.

A rack of feathers bound to a long rod on cords of unequal length, the feathers catching and holding lamplight in their barbs so each one glows differently, the rod hanging at a slight angle with one end propped on a wooden pin.

Seed-pods on single strings drifting steadily sideways against the draught rather than with it, each pod a different length of cord, so they hang at five distinct heights, one string left bare where its pod was removed and the hook kept waiting.

A long trailing vine looped over two rafters at different heights, its shrivelled leaves gone to pale papery translucence, and at the very end one impossible fresh bloom fully open and faintly luminous, the vine swaying in a slow arc.

Cluster of beeswax bags at three heights on the same line, each bag glowing softly from whatever is pressed inside it, the light ranging from warm gold to pale green across the row, one bag turned face-inward so its glow bleeds through the seam.

A row of small woven baskets on individual hooks, one lifting a hand's breadth higher than all the rest as though rising slowly, the lifted basket tilted so a thin line of amber light spills from its weave across the baskets below.

A long chain of dried caps strung on silver wire in an uneven diagonal across the ceiling, each cap holding an ember of orange light at its centre, the wire bowing lower at one end where the caps are densest and the light thickest.

A hoop wound with twine and hung with caged wisps at mismatched heights, their pale green light swinging in slow ellipses across the surrounding bundles, one cage on the hoop held shut with a bit of crooked wire twisted twice over.

Bundles of roots and dried bulbs in odd groupings of two and four and one, at three distinct heights on the same beam, each bundle leaking a faint mineral smell that seems to carry a pale shimmer visible in low light, one bundle smaller than a fist.

A drying rack on four twisted cords at uneven tensions so it hangs rhomboid, its trays of petals gone translucent in rose and amber and a blue so pale it reads as white, one tray propped level on a short stick jammed beneath its rim.

Sheaves of dried herbs in clusters of odd numbers along a thick cord strung rafter to rafter at a shallow diagonal, each sheaf tied with a different coloured thread, the seed-ends glowing faint gold where the lamplight catches resin, one sheaf tied with a ribbon clearly borrowed from elsewhere.

A braid of stems and grasses twisted into a slow spiral along the peak of the ceiling, small ember-lit caps woven into it at irregular intervals, the braid rotating a quarter-turn over the course of an hour, one end left loose and fraying into separate strands.

A braid of silver bulbs looped across the widest beam, each bulb holding a bright spark at its heart so the whole length pulses like a slow breath, one bulb wrapped in a mismatched ribbon of red where the braid was repaired.

A net of luminous spore-sacs stretched corner to corner, breathing faintly brighter and dimmer in a rhythm nothing else in the room shares, one dried cap fallen from a nearby string and caught in the mesh at an odd angle.

Bundles of upside-down stems still budding again in the warmth overhead, pale green shoots pushing between the twine at the tips, the tallest bundle hung a full hand's breadth lower than the rest on a longer cord.

A long chain of dried moon-shaped caps thinning to translucent slivers at one end, the thicker caps amber and opaque, the slivers glowing like rice-paper held to flame, the chain drifting a slow quarter-turn against the draught.

Garlands of berries looped at three uneven heights above the worktable, each berry glowing red from within like a banked coal, the lowest garland sagging where an extra cluster was added and never rebalanced.

Sheaves of grass tied at the culm, their seed-heads sparking soft gold whenever the air shifts, hung in an odd cluster of five at mismatched lengths, the shortest sheaf propped out from the beam on a short twig to keep it clear.

A mat of drying moss suspended on a flat frame of green-wood, tiny mushrooms sprouting white along its rim as it dries, one corner of the frame lifted higher than the others on a knotted cord that was not trimmed even.

A rope of knotted roots looping from rafter to rafter, one knot glowing amber where it was tied as though the light was folded in with the fibre, the rest of the rope dark and fragrant and swaying very slightly.

Strips of bark on a single long line, each strip curling and uncurling gently as though remembering the tree, their inner faces pale silver, hung at intervals that grow wider toward the far end where one hook was left bare.

Bundles wrapped in birch-bark cones, a thread of gold light leaking from each tip and throwing a tiny bright circle on whatever is above, the bundles hung in a cluster of seven at four different heights with no two at the same level.

A swag of flowers frozen mid-fall on their stems, petals arrested at the moment of opening, the whole swag faintly violet in colour and giving off a cold light that is bluer at the centre of each bloom.

A hanging tray of seed-pods on short strings, all drifting slowly sideways together against the draught as though agreeing on something, the tray itself canted on one side where the cord was knotted crooked and never corrected.

Thistle-heads on a line of fine wire, each one holding a faint blue static that makes the spines lean toward the neighbour closest to it, the line hung lower at one end so the thistles step downward in uneven increments.

A chain of apple-rings gone amber-transparent like small lenses, each ring holding the shadow of its core, three rings clustered close together and then a long gap before the last two, the final ring tagged with a blank scrap of bark.

Beeswax bags hung on a curved rod, each bag glowing softly gold with whatever is sealed inside, the bags in an odd grouping of six at different heights, the outermost bag on the left drifted half a span out of line.

A rack of feathers on a flat lath, the feathers catching the lamplight and holding it a moment longer than they should, shimmering copper and teal along their vanes, the lath propped at a slight tilt on a wedge of cork at one end.

A long swag of dried vine still carrying one fresh impossible bloom at the trailing end, its petals white and open, giving off a slow pulse of pale light every few breaths, the swag looped twice around one beam before it falls free.

A row of small baskets at uneven heights, herbs pressing up through their open weave in tight dry cushions, one basket riding a full hand's breadth above its hook on a twist of cord that has stretched and lifted it over time.

A cluster of translucent dried caps threaded on copper wire into a rough globe, each cap lit from inside with a dim orange ember, the globe turning on its own axis very slowly with the heat rising from the lamp beneath.

A braid of purple-flowered stems on a broad wooden hoop, the whole thing rotating in a long lazy turn like a mobile in a slow current, the stems darkening toward the centre of each flower where the colour went deepest in drying.

Bundles of dried silverweed tied with twine and hung at four heights in a loose vertical stack, each bundle glowing faintly at the cut end where the stems were trimmed, the lowest bundle tied with a mismatched length of blue ribbon.

A line of small caged wisps on iron hooks across the main beam, the wisps bobbing at different heights inside their cages and casting restless green shadows upward onto the underside of the rafter above them, one cage left empty and open.

Seed-pods strung on a long cord that sags in a deep curve between two hooks, the pods drifting sideways in slow unison, each one faintly luminous along its seam as though the light inside pressed outward trying to split the shell.

A tangle of dried root-slices on overlapping strings at three heights, the slices pale and semi-transparent where they thinned, catching light and throwing small warm circles on the ceiling above them, one string knotted twice where it had snapped and been repaired.

A wide hank of grasses and dried moon-caps woven together into a loose ceiling garland, the caps holding their ember-glow and the grass seed-heads sparking between them in gold when the air moves, the whole garland tagged at one end with a small painted picture of a crescent.
